newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Anwar says ringgit seen as stable at current level.
newsitem.headline: Anwar says ringgit seen as stable at current level.

text.p: Malaysian Deputy Prime Minister and Finance Minister Anwar Ibrahim said on Wednesday that the ringgit was "stable" at its current level.
"At the current level it is seen as stable," he told reporters when asked about the current strength of the currency against the dollar.
Asked whether the government was worried the strong ringgit might hurt exports, he replied: "As long as it is stable it is fine."
Asked about central bank, Bank Negara's possible intervention to slow the ringgit's rise, Anwar said: "You must understand that the stability of the ringgit is paramount.
"It could be slightly lower or higher but it's a stable currency."
He said market intervention by the central bank is "within the competence of the cnetral bank. It's part of the monetary policy."
He added that the ringgit is considered a stable currency throughout the year.
Anwar was speaking to reporters after an official function at his ministry.
The ringgit on Monday surged to a 17-month high against the dollar, rising as high as 2.4690 a dollar.
Dealers attributed the surge to buying by U.S. and Japanese for capital gains and to take advantage of Malaysia's relatively high interest rates.
Around 0925 GMT, ringgit was at 2.4757/67 a dollar against 2.4821/28 at the close of Kuala Lumpur trading on Tuesday.
